goal: I can find both measures of one rectangle and write each as a formula
opens: Stretch 10's judged items answered, 5 min. Then teaching first, 20 min: build one rectangle with tiles together, count both measures, write A = l × w and P = l + w + l + w, then 2 × (l + w); then pairs build their own rectangle from the same tiles and check that both forms of P agree
holds: Teacher, grid and tiles; students build along
by_hand: Three rectangles on grid paper, both equations for each, 15 min; wrong examples A and B fixed, 5 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned question

goal: I can find a missing side from the area or the perimeter
opens: Teaching first: two worked examples, 10 min
holds: Squares and fence, faded by the tool
tool_use: the five notes, show why, 20 min; on your own, check unaided, 5 min
by_hand: Each equation copied on paper. Then 15 min: wrong examples C and D fixed, two missing sides alone, checked by a partner; 5 min pulling the two together

goal: I can use both formulas with no picture, with big sides and fraction sides
opens: Teaching first, 10 min: one perimeter with multi-digit sides, the sum added to itself; one perimeter with fraction sides
holds: Students; sketches, no grid
by_hand: Five new wrong answers to fix, one for each error A to E, 12 min; then the mixed generator sheet, twelve problems, 22 min

goal: I can decide which measure a real problem needs
opens: Task, 10 min: "36 feet of fence. Which pen gives a dog the most room?" Close it with: every pen's length plus width is 18, half of 36. Then teaching first, 10 min: one "times as long" problem and one two-step problem (find a side, then the other measure)
holds: Students
by_hand: Six mixed problems with no cue words, two of them "times as long"; written task

goal: I can show what I know and fix what I missed
opens: End check, 30 min
holds: None
by_hand: Mark, 5 min; then groups by error
check_min: end check 30; respond 20; items 5 and 6 together 10 (the next stretch's readiness check when it exists)

goal: I can build and draw "4 times as many" and say it in a sentence
opens: Readiness results in hand; item 1 gaps go to day 81's reteach. Teaching first, 10 min: 3 cubes, then 4 times as many beside 4 more, each said in the frame "__ is __ times as many as __", which stays on the wall all stretch; say once that "times" also means occasions
holds: Teacher for ten minutes, then pairs with cubes
by_hand: Pairs build with cubes, then draw as strips, six comparisons, the frame filled in for each, 25 min; wrong examples A and D fixed, 10 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned question. Cubes are put away at the end of the day; a room with no cubes draws squares on paper

goal: I can read a multiplication equation as a comparison, two ways
opens: Reteach for readiness item 1, 5 min: whole class if many missed it; otherwise a small group in the warm-up, and these 5 min show the wrong example of E80's commonest error (A or D) beside the right one; if both are needed, E80's error is talked through inside the notice task. Then a notice task, 8 min: "What do you notice about 3 strips of 4 and 4 strips of 3?", with yesterday's strips; then the teacher ties the strips to 12 = 3 × 4, 3 min
holds: Students for the notice task; the teacher ties the strips to the equation
tool_use: Read it both ways, practise with feedback, 8 min
by_hand: Paper path while the tool is spec only, in the same 8 min: three equation cards, the first read aloud both ways as the model; students finish both sentences for each and check against the key on the screen. Then six equations, two sentences and one strip picture each, 15 min; wrong example C fixed, 6 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned question

goal: I can write the equation for a "times as many" sentence, quickly and correctly
opens: E81 back, 3 min: if many wrote one sentence or swapped the roles (C), C's wrong example again, pointing to the longer strip first; otherwise one student reads both sentences for their strip. Then teaching first, 5 min: three sentences turned into equations, one with 10 times, one about a length
holds: Students; a strip drawn only when a sentence is hard
by_hand: The sentence set on paper: sixteen, sentence to equation and equation to sentence, mixed, things counted and things measured, in four sets of four, each set checked against the key on the screen before the next, 28 min; written task, 9 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned question

goal: I can tell "times as many" from "more than" and draw each
opens: Reteach for readiness item 2, 5 min: whole class if many missed it; otherwise a small group in the warm-up, and these 5 min go to E82: if many wrote an addition (A), A's wrong example again; if many multiplied the rope lengths (B), reread the sentence and ask who has more. Then teaching first, 8 min: one story told both ways, "more than" and "times as many", two strip pictures
holds: Teacher, then students
tool_use: Growing, with the comparison switch, show why, 15 min
by_hand: Paper path while the tool is spec only, in the same 15 min: a table on the board, starting amounts 1, 4, 5 and 10, a column for "3 more" and one for "3 times as many"; students write each row on paper before it is filled in, then answer the planned question. Then four pairs of stories, each drawn both ways, 12 min; the "times more than" talk (E), 5 min; wrong example A fixed: "Bo has 4 stamps. Cy has 10 times as many. Cy has 14", beside 40, 5 min

goal: I can solve a comparison problem when the bigger or the smaller amount is missing
opens: E83 back, 3 min: if many gave both children the same answer or swapped them (A), draw both strips for one story and pick the one the words say; if many drew an extra copy (D), count the copies aloud. Then teaching first, 10 min: one story with the larger amount unknown, then the same story with the smaller amount unknown; the routine named: read, draw two strips, letter on the unknown, equation, solve, answer in a sentence, reread
holds: Teacher for ten minutes, then students
by_hand: Six problems, three with the larger amount unknown and three with the smaller, each with strips, a letter equation and a sentence answer, 25 min; wrong example B fixed, 7 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned question

goal: I can find how many times as many one amount is as another
opens: E84 back, 3 min: if many multiplied (B) or subtracted (A), ask "who has more?" and mark the longer strip before any numbers. Then teaching first, 5 min: a new story like yesterday's, with the number of times unknown. The warm-up today and tomorrow holds one grade 3 two-step problem
holds: Teacher for five minutes, then pairs
by_hand: Six problems, the unknown in each of the three places, 18 min; discussion, 7 min: two strip pictures for one problem, every copy drawn and one long strip marked with the times, each tied to the equation; pairs write one problem for another pair and solve the one they get, 8 min; wrong example C fixed: "Ann has 24 pens and Raj has 3. Raj has 8 times as many as Ann", beside the right sentence, 5 min; 4 min pulling it together

goal: I can decide what kind of comparison a problem is, then solve it
opens: E85 back, 3 min: if many swapped the roles (C), say the answer as a full sentence and test it on the strips. Then teaching first, 5 min: two problems that look alike and are not
holds: Students; a strip drawn only when stuck
tool_use: Which one?, practise with feedback, 20 min
by_hand: Paper path while the tool is spec only, in the same 20 min: sort cards, eight problems, three of them "more than"; for each card the student says what the strip would look like, drawing it only when stuck, then sorts it into "times as many" or "more than", and checks the sort against the key on the screen. Then four of the sorted problems solved on paper, each with a letter equation and a sentence answer, checked by a partner, 10 min; written task, 10 min

goal: I can solve a two-step problem with one equation and a letter, and check my answer with an estimate
opens: Reteach for readiness item 3, 5 min: whole class if many missed it; otherwise a small group in the warm-up, and these 5 min go to E86: if many multiplied (B) or mixed the two kinds (A), redraw both strips for the pumpkin and the squash. Then teaching first, 10 min: one story as two equations, then as one, the letter named in words first
holds: Teacher for ten minutes, then students
by_hand: Six two-step problems, three with a "times as many" step, the letter named and an estimate beside each answer, 17 min; three finished answers judged by estimate before anyone computes, 5 min; wrong examples F, G and H fixed, 6 min; written task, 5 min

goal: I can show what I know about "times as many" and two-step problems
opens: End check, 30 min
holds: None
by_hand: Mark, 5 min; then groups by error, 15 min, with the E87 slips handed back at the door so their errors join the F to H group; then stretch 11's readiness check, 10 min. Items 7 and 8 are judged after class and answered on day 89
check_min: end check 30; respond 20; stretch 11's readiness check 10

goal: I can add big numbers in columns and say what each small 1 is worth
opens: Readiness items 1 and 2 were given on day 71 and marked; their gaps go to day 73's reteach. Teaching first, 15 min: 3,746 + 2,538 in expanded form beside the standard algorithm, under place names, each carry said by its value ("14 ones is 1 ten and 4 ones"; "12 hundreds is 1 thousand and 2 hundreds"); then 1,895 + 4,368 the same way, the class saying each carry and "one what?" asked at every small 1
holds: Teacher for fifteen minutes; then pairs, both methods side by side
by_hand: Pairs do two sums both ways, expanded form beside the algorithm, 10 min; then four- and five-digit sums on grid paper with the algorithm alone, each small 1 labelled with its worth, 15 min; wrong examples A and D fixed (the teaching sum shown as 6,274 and as "512714"), 5 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned question

goal: I can line up numbers of different lengths, carry more than once, and check with an estimate
opens: Reteach for readiness items 1 and 2, 5 min: whole class if many missed them (467 + 285 in expanded form on a place value chart, then in columns; a number read by its comma groups); otherwise a small group in the warm-up, and these 5 min go to E72: if many lost a carry (A) or wrote a two-digit sum in one column (D), that wrong example again, each carry said by its value; if many answered "a 1" (C), students name each carry aloud all day; if both are needed, E72's error is talked through inside the worked sum. Then teaching first, 5 min: 6,285 + 947, an estimate first (about 6,300 + 900 = 7,200), both numbers said aloud, then lined up by place
holds: Students; expanded form gone; place names up, then taken down before E73
by_hand: Sums to six digits and of different lengths, an estimate before each, checked against the key on the screen every third sum, 22 min (place names come down after the first set); wrong examples B and E fixed, each beside its estimate, 6 min; written task, 7 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned questions

goal: I can subtract in columns when one place needs ungrouping, and say what I ungrouped
opens: Readiness items 3 and 4, written, 5 min, marked while students work the first difference. E73 back, 3 min: if many lined up from the left (B) or lost the last carry (E), that wrong example beside its estimate; otherwise one student reads their estimate and sum. Then teaching first, 10 min: 9,372 − 4,156 in expanded form beside the standard algorithm, under place names, 7 tens and 2 ones rewritten as 6 tens and 12 ones and said aloud: ungrouping is carrying run backwards, and the top number keeps its value
holds: Teacher for ten minutes; then pairs, both methods side by side
by_hand: Pairs do two differences both ways, expanded form beside the algorithm, 10 min; then four- and five-digit differences on grid paper, one ungrouping each, the ungrouped place said aloud, 12 min; wrong examples F and G fixed, 5 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned question

goal: I can ungroup more than once, in numbers up to six digits, and check by adding
opens: Reteach for readiness items 3 and 4, 5 min: whole class if many missed them (734 − 258 with 700 + 30 + 4 rewritten as 600 + 120 + 14, then in columns; 402 said as 3 hundreds, 9 tens, 12 ones); otherwise a small group in the warm-up, and these 5 min go to E74: if many took the smaller digit from the larger (F), F's wrong example again with "can I take 8 from 2?" asked in every column; if many left the tens as they were (G), G's wrong example in expanded form beside the algorithm; if both, F first and G inside the worked difference. Then teaching first, 5 min: 52,413 − 17,256, three ungroupings, an estimate first (about 52,000 − 17,000 = 35,000), checked by adding
holds: Students; expanded form gone; place names up, then taken down before E75
by_hand: Differences to six digits and of different lengths, an estimate before each and each checked by adding, checked against the key on the screen every third difference, 29 min (place names come down after the first set); wrong examples B and H fixed: B as 45,206 − 3,874 shown as 6,466 beside an estimate (it is 41,332), H as in the register, 6 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned question

goal: I can subtract when the top number has zeros
opens: E75 back, 3 min: if many forgot a place was already made smaller (H) or took the smaller digit from the larger (F), H's wrong example again, ungrouping everything first, then subtracting; if many lined up from the left (B), B's again beside its estimate; otherwise one student reads their estimate and check. Then teaching first, 10 min, expanded form back for zeros only: 402 − 178, with 402 renamed as 3 hundreds, 9 tens, 12 ones before any column; then 6,005 − 2,347, renamed in one line as 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 15 ones. Students who missed readiness item 4 sit with the teacher for both
holds: Teacher for ten minutes, then students
by_hand: Differences with one, two and three zeros in the top number, and from 100,000, the top number renamed in one line before any column, each checked by adding, 20 min; wrong example I fixed, 5 min; written task, 7 min; 5 min pulling it together with the planned question

goal: I can add and subtract big numbers without help
opens: E76 slips back at the door: a student who made I or F joins that group in the respond half. The mixed set, 10 min, takes the place of the next readiness check, which is given on day 79 because Check 2 comes first. Then the end check, 30 min
holds: Students alone
tool_use: Trip ledger, practise with feedback, 10 min
by_hand: Paper path while the tool is spec only, in the same 10 min: the day 77 mixed set, five sums and five differences to six digits, two of them across zeros, each checked against the key on the screen as soon as it is done, a right-first-try count kept by the student. Mark, 5 min; then groups by error, 15 min: A to E do their "if many" action, and B and F to I do theirs; a student in two groups goes to the subtracting one. Items 9.1c and 9.2c are judged after class and handed back on day 79, after Check 2

goal: I can show what I know about fractions, decimals and big numbers
opens: Check 2, one period, alone, on paper. It covers stretches 6 to 9 (a fraction times a whole number, decimals, place value to a million, adding and subtracting) and fractions again, weighted to major work: a part built from the generators and two fixed tasks that ask for an explanation or a model, with a scoring guide (spine). Stretch 9's share is items C2.1 and C2.2; stretches 6 to 8 add theirs when they are planned, and the two fixed tasks are chosen then
holds: Students alone
by_hand: No respond half: Check 2 is marked and judged after class, and day 79 responds. Day 77's judged items wait for day 79 too

goal: I can fix what I missed on Check 2
opens: Items 9.1c and 9.2c back, 5 min: the "meets" answers of both shown, students fix their own in pen, marks on stretch 9's record sheet; a student missing a look-for joins that item's group (9.1c to the E group, which estimates first; 9.2c to the H group, which checks by adding). Check 2's keyed items marked against the key on the screen, pen down, 5 min; hands up by item set the groups
holds: Students in groups by error; the teacher sits with the largest group
by_hand: Groups by error, 30 min: stretch 9's groups do their error's "if many" action from the register, with new numbers; groups for stretches 6 to 8 follow those stretches' plans when they are written; a student in no group does the extension (a difference from 1,000,000 by way of 999,999). Then E79, 5 min. Then stretch 10's readiness check, the last 10 min (courses/math-4/u10-1/readiness.md). E79 is read that night and goes to the warm-up, where adding and subtracting with the standard algorithm stay to day 150: a student who made I or F has their warm-up differences across zeros checked by the teacher on days 80 to 82
check_min: warm-up 5; items back and marking 10; groups by error 30; exit 5; stretch 10's readiness check 10
